en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from al Qasim Al Nahdy, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Al Kunasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

Once ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> went outside (the town) with him<sup>asws</sup> was a man from the sons of Al-Zubeyr who was saying (believing) in his<sup>asws</sup> Imamate. So they encamped in an oasis from those oasis beneath a dry palm tree which had dried from the drought.

So it was furnished (carpeted) for Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> beneath the palm tree, and its was furnished for Al-Zubeyri by the side beneath another palm tree. So Al-Zubeyri said, and raised his head, ‘If only there were dates in this palm tree, we could have eaten from it’. So Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘And you are desiring the dates?’ So Al-Zubeyri said, ‘Yes’.

He (Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> raised his<sup>asws</sup> hands towards the sky and supplicated with a speech which he did not understand, and the palm tree turned green. Then it came to be to its state whereby it sprouted leaves and bore fruit. So the cameleer whom they had hired camels from, said, ‘Sorcery, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!’ So Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you! It isn’t sorcery. But, a supplication of the son<sup>asws</sup> of a Prophet<sup>azwj</sup> that is Answered’.
So, they climbed up the palm tree and they picked whatever was in it, and it sufficed them’.
